baslik: Motoseyir — The motorcyclist’s sat nav for twisty roads
aciklama: Motoseyir is a motorcycle sat nav that plans by distance, not by minutes. Back roads, coast and enduro modes, a tour generator, 1,600+ mountain passes, group rides and CarPlay.
og_baslik: Motoseyir — The motorcyclist’s sat nav for twisty roads
og_aciklama: Distance-first routing, back roads, a tour generator, 1,600+ mountain passes, group rides, intercom and CarPlay — in one app.
jsonld_aciklama: Distance-first navigation app for motorcyclists: shortest route, back roads, tour generator, mountain passes, group riding, intercom, CarPlay and legendary routes.
jsonld_ucretsiz: Unlimited routing and navigation in Türkiye, Europe and the USA, 1 saved tour; Pro’s 3-month and yearly plans include a 7-day free trial outside Türkiye, for new subscribers.
jsonld_pro: AI CoRider, CarPlay, group creation and intercom, Discover, tour generator, unlimited tours and trails, Back roads and Coast modes and best order for multiple stops.
hero_alt: A motorcyclist riding a twisty mountain road along the coast in the light of sunset
hero_lead: Motoseyir plans by distance, not by minutes. Back roads, coast or enduro, you choose. Or tell it which way you want to ride and let it build the tour; or pick a mountain pass and go.
hero_micro: Routing and navigation are free and unlimited in Türkiye, Europe and the USA; no account needed.
s2_t: legendary roads of Türkiye, Europe and the USA, ready as routes
s3_t: your route on the car screen, full screen
s4_t: same route, talking as you ride
k1_alt: Navigation screen in Motoseyir: next turn, distance left and speed
k1_p: It compares the alternatives between the same two points and suggests the shortest. On a multi-stop tour it works out the order of the stops, too. The rest is up to you.
k1_a_d: The default; it goes by kilometres.
k1_b_d: Leaves the main road for the twisty ones.
k1_c_d: Looks for gravel and unpaved roads.
k2_alt: Tour generator screen: direction and duration dial
k2_h2: Pick a direction and a time, the tour is ready.
k2_p: Turn the dial to the way you want to go and choose how many hours you have. Motoseyir draws a tour in that direction; you see it on the map and start if you like it.
k3_alt: Mountain passes screen: a map of Alpine passes with an altitude list
k3_p: Every pass has its altitude and exact location, and most have photos. Passes that close in winter show the months they’re closed, and dirt roads are marked as dirt. Add the ones you like to your tour and go.
k4_alt: AI CoRider screen: planner and chat options
k4_p: You talk, your hands stay on the bars. No reaching for the phone to ask something, add a stop or plan a break.
k5_alt1: Group ride screen: the route on the map and the next turn
k5_alt2: Motoseyir navigation on a CarPlay screen
k5_h2: Ride as a group, talking as you go.
k5_p: Take the same route as your friends and see everyone on the map. Joining a group by invite or code is free.
k5_a_d: Meeting point, live location, one route.
k5_b_d: Talk to the group while you ride; no extra hardware.
k5_c_d: Your route on the car screen; the phone stays in your pocket.
k6_alt: Discover screen: stops along the route and their list
k6_p: See the back roads, beach roads, campsites and places to eat along your route, and add the ones you like.
k7_alt: A sample from a trip map video: the Istanbul–Athens route
k7_h2: The road you rode stays with you.
k7_p: Record the ride, watch it again later, and turn it into a trip map video to share.
k7_a_d: Watch the way you rode again on the map.
k7_b_d: Turn your tour into a short video.
k7_c_d: If rain is forecast at your stops, you see it on the route.
k7_d_d: Bring the route you already have into the app.
k8_alt: The motorcycle that stands for you on the map; drag left or right to turn it
k8_p: While you ride, a marker stands for you on the map. You pick it from the grid in Settings: bike, chopper, maxi scooter, touring, arrow or helmet.
k9_alt: Legendary roads screen: a list of ready-made routes and their map
k9_p: The famous roads of Türkiye, Europe and the USA come as ready-made routes: Tail of the Dragon, Beartooth Highway, Big Sur and more. Pick one and go.
k10_p: What’s inside the app, in two minutes.
fiyat_h2: Free to ride, Pro when you want more.
plan_u_p: Route planning and turn-by-turn navigation are unlimited in Türkiye, Europe and the USA. No account needed; the free tier keeps 1 saved tour.
plan_p_p: The 3-month and yearly plans start with a 7-day free trial outside Türkiye, for new subscribers. Pro unlocks:
pp6: Back roads and Coast modes, best order for multiple stops
fiyat_not: Current prices vary by region; you see them on the subscription screen in the App Store. Cancel anytime in your App Store account.
y118_1: Fixed a crash when switching from Blog to Feed in Community.
y118_2: Recording a video of your 3D ride replay starts more reliably.
y118_3: “Ready” no longer shows before the map has loaded, and the camera no longer jumps when you finish a pinch zoom.
y117_1: Trip map: watch a long tour or ride as a video on a clean map. As your route draws itself, the towns you passed and your photos appear one by one.
y117_2: New shortcuts on the Start screen: home and work, record a ride, a one-hour loop from here, a legendary road nearby.
y117_3: 298 mountain passes and six new legendary roads in the USA, and Coastal mode now works across Europe too.
y117_4: “Get to know Motoseyir” in Settings is a short video tour of the app, tab by tab.
y116_1: Watch in 3D: replay a recorded ride as if you were following from a helicopter; your photos pop up where you took them.
y116_2: Share as video: make a 15, 30 or 60-second vertical video, ready for Instagram. No Pro needed.
y116_3: Ride analysis: moving time, real breaks, sharp curves, total climb, and how much of the road was new to you.
y116_4: In Tour Generator, “Another one” brings three new loops on different roads, and you can avoid highways, tolls and dirt roads.
v_yuksek_h: The five highest in the US, all in Colorado
v_n1_d: The OpenStreetMap point that marks the pass. It sits on the road at the summit, not at an encyclopedia’s rough coordinate.
v_n2_d: From the pass’s Wikipedia or Wikidata entry, or OpenStreetMap when there isn’t one. It’s the road’s highest point.
v_n3_d: From the road’s seasonal closure tag in OpenStreetMap. If your tour crosses a pass that may be closed that month, the app tells you.
v_n4_d: Passes you ride over are ticked off from your ride log automatically. No internet needed.
v_atif: Location and closure data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Photos from Wikimedia Commons; each one shows its author and licence in the app.
